h1:
The Pathio Tree Tunnel
A Seaside Road Where the Trees Arch Into a Tunnel
intro: If you drive the coastal road around Pak Nam Chumphon near Khao Matsee, you'll hit a stretch where the pines on both sides lean in until they form a green tunnel, with sunlight filtering down through the leaves. It's a newer check-in spot that locals are proud of and travelers are just starting to find. Over on the Pathio side there's Baan OuadChum, a seaside treehouse cafe built around big old trees — so you can pack both of Chumphon's tree spots into one trip. Here's the location, the best times to shoot, and the nearby stops to make planning easy.

blocks.html: When people talk about the "Chumphon tree tunnel," they actually mean two places on opposite sides of the province. The first is the pine tunnel on the coastal road in Pak Nam Chumphon, near Khao Matsee — a natural stretch of road where the pines on both sides have grown until their branches curve in to meet overhead in a green canopy. Drive through and it feels like passing under an arch of leaves. The other is Baan OuadChum, a seaside treehouse cafe in Pathio district designed around big trees. This guide covers both, plus nearby stops you can string together into a single trip.

blocks.text: The Pine Tunnel on the Pak Nam Chumphon Coastal Road

blocks.html: The main spot for the tree tunnel is on the coastal road in Pak Nam Chumphon, around the foot of Khao Matsee in Pak Nam subdistrict, Mueang Chumphon district. This is a row of sea pines planted along both sides of the road years ago, and now that they've grown to full height the branches lean in and meet over the middle of the road in a long tunnel. Drive or cycle through and it feels noticeably shadier and cooler than out in the open. It's a new landmark that Pak Nam locals love bringing people to photograph, about 15 min from Chumphon town.

items: Location — the coastal road in Pak Nam Chumphon at the foot of Khao Matsee, Pak Nam subdistrict, Mueang Chumphon (search the map for "Khao Matsee Viewpoint," then follow the coastal road)
Best time to shoot — early morning, when the low sun streams through the leaves, or late afternoon before dusk for soft light and fewer people than midday
Entry fee — none, it's a public road; you can park on the shoulder to shoot, but watch for oncoming traffic
Time needed — 20–30 min is plenty to grab the tunnel shot and the sea view right beside it

blocks.title: Straight talk before you go
blocks.html: This is a working road that locals actually use, with cars passing the whole time — it's not a closed lot where you can stand in the middle for long. Time your shots, check both directions first, and don't linger in the lane. In the rainy season the trees get dense and the surface turns slippery. If you really want good light, come morning or evening and skip midday, when the sun is overhead and hot.

blocks.text: Touring Pak Nam by Local Saleng Three-Wheeler

blocks.html: The charm of the Pak Nam side is that you can see it the community way. Locals run saleng (sidecar three-wheelers) that take you around several spots in Pak Nam Chumphon in one loop — the pine tunnel, the viewpoint, and the fishing way of life. The ride runs about 300 THB per vehicle, seats around 3 people, and takes roughly 2 hours. It's an easy way to get around and chat with locals along the way. If you'd rather not drive yourself or you're a small group, this is good value and genuinely fun. Ask about the queue at the Pak Nam community tourism point.

items.name: Khao Matsee Viewpoint
items.blurb: A hilltop above Pak Nam with 360-degree views of the sea, the fishing village, and the islands. The landmark is a statue of Guan Yin (Avalokitesvara). Open roughly 06:00–19:00 — come in the evening for the sunset and the lights of the fishing boats.

items.name: Phra Rot Beach / Pak Nam Sea
items.blurb: The beach and shoreline right along the coastal road. Walk and catch the breeze, and shoot the sea alongside the pine tunnel in a single stop.

items.name: Pak Nam Fishing Village
items.blurb: A fresh seafood market and waterfront seafood restaurants, near the pier for boats to Koh Tao and Koh Phangan. A good spot for lunch or dinner after your photos.

blocks.text: Baan OuadChum, the Treehouse Cafe on the Pathio Side

blocks.html: The other tree spot in Chumphon that gets a lot of talk is Baan OuadChum Treehouse, a cafe and community space in Pathio district. It's built with houses and wooden walkways around big old trees, with balcony corners and leafy nooks where you can sip coffee and take in the view. It's a shady, photogenic stop, and if you're exploring the northern side around Thung Wua Laen or Khao Dinso it's an easy add-on. It sits behind King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang, Chumphon Campus (Pathio).

items: Location — behind KMITL Chumphon Campus (Ladkrabang Pathio), Pathio district, Chumphon
Hours — roughly 08:00–20:00 (Tuesdays open in the afternoon; hours can change, so check the cafe's page before you go)
Prices — coffee and drinks start in the low hundreds of THB; snacks and food menu available
Contact — call 092-895-2218 (confirm opening days and seating before a holiday)

blocks.title: Photo tips
blocks.html: The tree tunnel looks best in low, angled light — line your camera up along the road so the pines sweep in as leading lines. A solid light-colored top stands out against the green of the leaves. At Baan OuadChum, the filtered light through the leaves and the wooden balcony work nicely; shoot mid-morning while the sun is still soft so you get the view without shooting into the glare.

blocks.text: Planning a Tree + Sea Trip in Chumphon Without Wearing Yourself Out

blocks.html: The Pak Nam pine tunnel is on the town side, while Baan OuadChum is up on the Pathio side to the north — a fair distance apart. Don't rush to cram it all into one day; pair each spot with its own zone instead. Here's a sample two-day plan that takes in both the trees and the sea at an easy pace — adjust the timing as needed.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Town side — pine tunnel, Khao Matsee, Pak Nam

items.activity: Head out of town to the Pak Nam coastal road and shoot the pine tunnel in the morning light
items.note: Morning sun streams through the leaves and crowds are thin

items.activity: Go up to Khao Matsee Viewpoint for 360-degree sea and village views, and pay respects to Guan Yin
items.note: The road up is steep — drive slowly

items.activity: Take a local saleng three-wheeler loop around Pak Nam, or walk the shore at Phra Rot Beach
Eat fresh seafood by the water at the Pak Nam fishing village
Head back up Khao Matsee or stay by the sea for the sunset and the fishing-boat lights
items.note: Evening is the most beautiful time

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Pathio side — Baan OuadChum + the northern coast

items.activity: Drive north to Pathio district and stop for a swim at Thung Wua Laen Beach
Visit Baan OuadChum, sip coffee, and shoot the trees and wooden balcony
items.note: Check the cafe's opening day first

items.activity: Have lunch by the beach in Pathio
Continue up to Khao Dinso for bay views, or visit Wat Khao Chedi for a 360-degree view
items.note: Pick one depending on your energy

items.activity: Catch the evening breeze by the sea before heading back to town

blocks.title: Getting there and parking
blocks.html: These spots are spread out and public transport is limited — having your own car or renting a car/motorbike in town is by far the easiest way around. The Pak Nam coastal road is narrow with traffic, so park where you won't block the way and don't stand in the middle of the road to shoot. The road up Khao Matsee is steep for about 800 m and the parking lot at the top is limited, so if it's busy you may have to wait for a spot.

faq.q: Where is the Chumphon tree tunnel?
faq.a: The most-photographed spot is the pine tunnel on the coastal road in Pak Nam Chumphon, at the foot of Khao Matsee in Pak Nam subdistrict, Mueang Chumphon district. Search the map for Khao Matsee Viewpoint, then follow the coastal road and you'll reach the stretch where the pines on both sides arch into a tunnel — about 15 min from town. The other tree spot is Baan OuadChum in Pathio district.

faq.q: What's the best time to photograph the tree tunnel?
faq.a: Early morning or late afternoon before dusk, when the angled light streams through the leaves and there are fewer people than midday. Skip midday, when the sun is overhead and hot. In the rainy season the trees get dense and the surface turns slippery, so take extra care.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for the tree tunnel, and how much is the saleng ride?
faq.a: The pine tunnel itself is a public road with no entry fee. If you want an easy loop around Pak Nam, locals run saleng three-wheelers that take you to several spots in one go — about 300 THB per vehicle, seating roughly 3 people, over about 2 hours.

faq.q: What time does Baan OuadChum open, and where is it?
faq.a: Baan OuadChum Treehouse is behind King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang, Chumphon Campus, in Pathio district. It opens roughly 08:00–20:00 (Tuesdays open in the afternoon, and hours can change). It's best to check the cafe's page or call 092-895-2218 before going on a holiday.

faq.q: How can I combine the tree tunnel with other places?
faq.a: On the town side you can pair the Pak Nam pine tunnel with Khao Matsee Viewpoint and seafood at the Pak Nam fishing village in a single morning. Baan OuadChum is on the Pathio side, so you can pair it with Thung Wua Laen Beach, Khao Dinso, or Wat Khao Chedi. Make it a two-day trip and you won't wear yourself out.
